claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor high-temperature oxygen resistance.
An aluminide-based surface coating will improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Aluminum supplied by the coating will diffuse into the alloy surface during high-temperature exposure.
The diffused aluminum will form a thin, continuous, dense, and adherent Al2O3 surface scale.
The Al2O3 scale will be slow-growing.
The Al2O3 scale will act as a diffusion barrier against oxygen ingress.
Suppressing oxygen ingress will reduce oxidation and oxygen penetration relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Because the coating is thin and surface-localized, it will have minimal influence on bulk ductility and yield strength.
After exposure at 1000 °C in ambient air for about 100 hours, coated specimens will retain yield strength similar to the untreated cast alloy.
After exposure at 1000 °C in ambient air for about 100 hours, coated specimens will retain ductility similar to the untreated cast alloy.
Oxidation of untreated HfNbTaTiZr in oxygen-containing high-temperature environments leads to degradation of its properties.
Coating uniformity and thickness may affect oxidation protection and mechanical performance.
The coating process may alter the near-surface microstructure or introduce residual stresses.
